Arrange

POST /boards/:id/arrange lays out cards that already exist and is how to tidy a board. The default, auto, lays each section out as its own block, notes in columns at their own size and pictures in rows at their true shape, sets the sections out near a screen's shape, and brings notes the API made earlier up to date. justified, masonry, grid, row and column are there by name; by hand, cards carry x, y, w, h, z, rotation and a group.

Updated October 27, 2026

Placing cards is half of an API that works. The other half is that what lands looks composed rather than spilled.

Automatic

curl -X POST https://clusters.soleilpictures.com/api/v1/boards/$BOARD/arrange \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer undefined…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'

Omit card_ids to arrange the whole board, or pass a subset to tidy part of it. Cards that aren't on the board ("unplaced": true) are left alone and take no room in the layout. The same layout works on adding cards and on import, so a batch can land arranged instead of needing a second call.

The layouts

auto · column · grid · justified · masonry · row

auto — the default. A board reads as its sections (groups), so each is laid out as a block of its own: pictures (images and videos) in rows across the block, flush on both edges and each at its true shape, under the section's palette if it has one; anything else in columns, each card at its own size, a picture at the column's width and a palette or a wide card across the top. The blocks are then set out in rows, in order, at the width that brings the whole board nearest 16:10 with its rows about as wide as each other. Cards in no section make one block more.

┌ CANON ──────────┐  ┌ JOURNAL ─────────────────┐
│ ┌─────┐ ┌─────┐ │  │ ┌─────┐ ┌─────┐ ┌─────┐  │
│ │     │ │     │ │  │ │     │ │     │ │     │  │
│ └─────┘ │     │ │  │ └─────┘ └─────┘ └─────┘  │
│ ┌─────┐ └─────┘ │  └──────────────────────────┘
│ └─────┘         │
└─────────────────┘

Cards are taken in reading order — top to bottom, each row left to right — unless order names the ones that come first, and a column fills in that same order, so arranging a board auto arranged moves nothing.

Notes brought up to date. Any arrange brings a note the API made before notes showed their title and color up to date: its title becomes its heading, its colour its fill, and its height its text's (see Notes). Only a note nobody has opened or resized in the app is touched, and one edited while the arrange runs keeps what was written there and is only moved. repaired counts them.

justified — rows of equal height, each picture at its true aspect ratio, flush on both edges. There are no holes in it, which is why it is the right answer for photographs.

┌────────┐┌───┐┌─────────┐
│        ││   ││         │
└────────┘└───┘└─────────┘
┌─────┐┌──────────┐┌─────┐
│     ││          ││     │
└─────┘└──────────┘└─────┘

masonry — columns of equal width, balanced by height, ordered by colour so the board reads as a deliberate palette sweep rather than as arrival order. Leaves a ragged bottom edge, which is the trade for never cropping anything.

grid — one uniform cell for everything, each card centred in its cell. The right answer for mixed kinds — an image beside a PDF beside an audio clip — where a shared cell reads as a clean matrix. For photographs of different shapes it leaves a hole around every portrait, which is what justified fixes.

row and column — a single line, cross-axis centred.

Groups stay together. With every layout, cards in a group are laid out a group at a time, each group as its own block with room for its outline and name; with the named ones the blocks are set out side by side (in one line for row and column). Cards in no group make one block more. Arranging a board that is already arranged moves nothing: auto and justified size each image from its own pixels, so a picture shows whole rather than cropped to the card it was given, and comes out the same size the next time.

Knobs

FieldMeaning
orderCard ids to put first, in this order; the rest follow in reading order.
gapSpace between cards. Default 24.
widthThe width the block is solved against, not auto. Omit it and a roughly square block is chosen from the number of items — a canvas has no edges, so there is no container to infer one from.
row_heightTarget row height. justified only.
columnsColumn cap. grid and masonry only.
dry_runCompute everything, write nothing.
card_idsArrange a subset. At most 1000 per call.

auto chooses its own widths, so it takes only order and gap.

The answer:

FieldMeaning
layoutThe layout used
arrangedHow many cards were laid out
repairedNotes the API made earlier, brought up to date
sectionsHow many sections the cards laid out are in
boundsx, y, w and h of the cards laid out
not_foundIds in card_ids that aren't on the board
cardsThose cards, as they now are

Two things worth knowing. auto and justified resize pictures — fitting a row to a width is a resize — and auto stretches a palette to its section's width; the other layouts only move cards. And a layout named on a card write arranges the whole batch including cards that carried their own x and y: "lay these out as rows" and "put this one at x=40" are contradictory, and the one you asked for by name wins.

By hand

Every card carries the full geometry:

FieldMeaning
x, yPosition, in canvas units
w, hSize
zStacking. Higher is in front; fractional values are fine
rotationDegrees
groupMembership of a group, by its name — made if the board has none
group_idMembership of a group, by its id
section_headerRender as a full-width heading

z was readable but not writable until now — you could see which of two overlapping cards was on top and had no way to swap them.

Groups

A group is how a board says these belong together: a labelled outline round a set of cards, which then move as one.

curl -X POST https://clusters.soleilpictures.com/api/v1/boards/$BOARD/groups \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer undefined…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "name": "Costume — Act II", "shape": "box" }'

The full set:

EndpointWhat it does
GET /boards/:id/groupsThe groups on a board
POST /boards/:id/groupsCreate one
PATCH /boards/:id/groups/:groupIdRename or restyle it
DELETE /boards/:id/groups/:groupIdUngroup — removes the group, never its cards

Pass the returned id as group_id on any card — or skip this step, and name the group in a card's group: the board's group of that name is used, or made with the cards (see Sections). shape is box (one rectangle round everything) or hug (following each card). Deleting a group ungroups; it never deletes the cards — there is no undo on an HTTP call, and a group holding forty cards must not be a way to lose forty cards.

Section headings

A card with section_header: true becomes a full-width heading, and if the board is published it renders as an <h2> in the article. Add sub for a line underneath. This is what turns a wall of references into something with a shape somebody else can read.

Frequently asked questions

How do I tidy a board an assistant made?

Call POST /boards/:id/arrange with nothing else, or arrange_board over MCP. auto lays each section out as a block of its own and sets the sections out in order, and the notes the API made earlier get their title shown, their colour painted and their height fitted to their text.

Can I choose what comes first?

Yes. Pass order, a list of card ids. Those cards come first, in that order, and the rest follow in reading order, top to bottom and left to right.

How do I make a dump of images look like a moodboard?

Pass layout when you import or add them, or call POST /boards/:id/arrange afterwards. auto and justified both give rows of pictures flush on both edges, every picture at its real aspect ratio; auto keeps each section to a block of its own.

Can I see where things would land before moving anything?

Yes. Pass dry_run and the response contains the computed positions with nothing written, so you can compare two layouts before touching a board.

Will arranging move my cards somewhere else on the canvas?

No. The block is re-anchored on its own current top-left, and pushed clear of any cards it is not moving, so tidying part of a board cannot bury the rest.

How do I say that a set of cards belongs together?

Name the section in group on each card, and the board's group of that name is used, or made with the cards. A group draws a labelled outline round its cards and moves them as one.
